correctness.rationale: Choose pairwise orthonormal (e_0,e_1,...) in infinite-dimensional real/complex H and z in the unit sphere of nonzero Banach X. Let R_n=e_n*⊗z. Compact S sends weakly null e_n to norm-null S e_n. For ||S||<=1 and x=a e_n+u with u perpendicular, Cauchy–Schwarz yields ||(S+R_n)x|| <= |a| ||z+S e_n|| + ||S|| sqrt(1-|a|^2) <= sqrt(||z+S e_n||^2+||S||^2); taking liminf/infn gives <=sqrt2. Rank-one S_0=e_0*⊗z satisfies ||S_0+R_n||=||e_0*+e_n*||=sqrt2 for all n, so supremum infimum is exactly sqrt2. This construction works over both scalar fields and even nonseparable H; no finite test or unsupported independent certification required.

value.rationale: A sharp norm value sqrt2 independent of target Banach space X supplies a quantitative gap 2-sqrt2 and an explicit countable rank-one witness for a natural operator-space geometric property. This is an exact structural obstruction, not a generic restatement that some sequence prevents octahedrality; the constant is attained simultaneously for all probes by one compact rank-one S_0. Its proof is elementary once the right witness is chosen, but the precise uniform sharp bound is mathematically motivated.
